show.name: Bell X1 | Good Bones Tour 2026
show.description:
Bell X1 are an Irish musical group, the members of which are Paul Noonan, Dave Geraghty and Dominic Phillips.

Formed in 1999, they have released 8 studio albums, 4 of which having been nominated for the Choice Music Prize. Over the past 2 decades they have become recognised as one of Ireland’s most popular live performers.

They are known for their versatile musical palette, lyrical dexterity and catalogue of popular singles. Their albums vary in sound and style, their range taking in pop, alternative, indie, hard rock, post-punk, acoustic, lo-fi, folk-rock, ballad, synth-pop, new wave and electronica.

With their signature blend of heartfelt lyrics, rich harmonies and inventive musicianship, this promises to be a magical live experience not to be missed.

show.name: Escape the Internet
show.description:
Part live show. Part big-screen game. Part interactive adventure. This is unlike anything we've hosted before.

Escape the Internet transforms Nerve Centre into a live cinematic game world, where the audience becomes part of the action.

Led by comedian, Lucas Rizzotto, you'll watch an animated story unfold on the big screen, but this isn't a show where you simply sit back and watch. Using your phone, you'll take part in games, make choices and interact with everyone else in the room as the story develops around you.

Expect big laughs, unexpected decisions, playful challenges and plenty of moments you'll want to talk about afterwards.

Come with friends or come on your own, the whole idea is to get a room full of people playing, laughing and connecting together. The experience has been designed around interactions that reveal a little about how you and the people around you think about everything from ethics to love.

You haven't experienced anything quite like this at Nerve Centre before. Are you ready to escape the internet?

show.name: Good Vibrations | Rip It Up
show.description:
Nerve Centre presents a special programme, Loud, Young and Free as part of Rip It Up, a UK-wide film season made possible with the support of the BFI Film Audience Network, awarding funds by The National Lottery.

Terri Hooley (Richard Dormer) is a radical, rebel and music-lover in 1970s Belfast, when the bloody conflict known as the Troubles shuts down his city. As all his friends take sides and take up arms, Terri opens a record shop on the most bombed half-mile in Europe and calls it Good Vibrations. Through it he discovers a compelling voice of resistance in the city’s nascent underground punk scene. Galvanizing the young musicians into action, he becomes the unlikely leader of a motley band of kids and punks who join him in his mission to create a new community, an Alternative Ulster, to bring his city back to life.

"So here I am once more..."

Marquee Square Heroes pay tribute to Marillion's years with Fish, recreating the powerful storytelling, atmosphere and musicianship that made the band one of the most distinctive names in British progressive rock.

Expect an unforgettable journey through the classic albums Script for a Jester's Tear, Fugazi, Misplaced Childhood and Clutching at Straws, performed with the passion, precision and attention to detail these extraordinary songs deserve.

Featuring experienced musicians from the progressive rock scene, including contemporaries from Marillion's legendary Marquee days, Marquee Square Heroes capture the drama, nostalgia and sheer power of this remarkable period in the band's history.

Whether you joined them last time or are seeing them for the first time, come and experience an evening dedicated to one of progressive rock's most iconic catalogues.

Welcome back to the circus...
